articles.title: From Grocery Lists to Gallery Walls: Marisa Aragón Ware’s Paper Sculptures Redefine the Everyday
articles.summary: Marisa Aragón Ware transforms ordinary paper into breathtakingly detailed sculptures of flora and fauna. Inspired by Colorado’s forests and the concept of biophilia, her work reminds us of our deep connection to nature. See her pieces at Arch Enemy Arts starting June 5.

articles.title: When Timbot Glitched, These MIT Students Turned a Tech Fail into a Teaching Moment
articles.summary: MIT’s FIRSTxMIT club built a robot in 72 hours and demoed it at the inaugural Governors Cup in D.C. When Wi-Fi failed, they switched to Ethernet—and high schoolers instantly related. The club aims to spread hands-on STEM inspiration nationwide.

articles.title: Supergirl’s Massive Practical Set Is a Hidden Ode to Artist Bilquis Evely
articles.summary: On the set of Supergirl, the sprawling war-torn town square is named Evely on the planet Bilquis—a direct tribute to comic artist Bilquis Evely. The production emphasizes practical effects and director Craig Gillespie’s vision, honoring the Woman of Tomorrow source material.
